subject: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Amira Patel <amira@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot

Hi Amira —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, Zenith wants the ability to swap traffic between our Compact (cost‑optimized) tier and the High‑Throughput tier during the 6‑week pilot window. To make that low friction for both teams I attached a short checklist (zenith_proposal_v2.pdf) and our feature matrix.

Key asks from your side so we can prepare:
- Expected % of traffic that would need to move to High‑Throughput during spike windows (approx. avg QPS).
- Are there specific endpoints (e.g., /chat, /embeddings) that must always run on High‑Throughput?
- Do you require historical logs retained for 90 days or longer (impacts storage pricing)?

A few notes on our end (so you can surface to procurement):
- We support one full tier switch per hour with an automated rollback window (30 minutes by default).
- If Zenith requests an emergency rollback outside that window we can execute a manual rollback; that triggers a short SLA exception and requires a signed amendment for guaranteed latency SLAs.
- For the pilot we can offer a one‑time 15% pilot credit on invoice if you commit to a 3‑month post‑pilot evaluation.

Ben is looped on the pricing mechanics; Lauren is on the contract side. If you can send the expected QPS and any retention constraints today, Ben will send a compact pricing model and a downgrade path with explicit credit math.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: zenith_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal outline, checklist)
Attachment: redwood_feature_matrix.xlsx (feature / tier mapping)
From: Amira Patel <amira@zenithhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot

Vivek —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick clarifications before I pass to procurement and engineering: 

1) The rollback window you mentioned — can that be shortened to 10 minutes for high‑risk endpoints? We have clinical triage flows where a problematic model response needs immediate mitigation.
2) The 15% pilot credit — is that applied to all usage during the pilot or only to the incremental cost when we move to High‑Throughput?
3) On retention: we need 90‑day logs for now but may request 1 year later. Will that change be a simple add‑on or require a contract amendment?

Ben/Redwood team — could you provide the downgrade math and a sample invoice line showing the pilot credit? Procurement will want to see exact terms before the PO.

Thanks,
Amira Patel
Director of Product, Zenith Health
amira@zenithhealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Amira Patel <amira@zenithhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot

Amira —

Short answers up front, then a worked example (see attached spreadsheet for line‑item math).

1) Rollback window: we can shorten the automated rollback to 10 minutes for identified endpoints. For the pilot we'll flag /chat/triage and /chat/diagnostics as protected — the control plane enforces the 10‑minute automated rollback for those routes. Manual rollbacks outside the automated window are allowed but we charge an operational fee ($250) if executed more than twice per month.

2) Pilot credit: the 15% pilot credit applies to total USD invoice for the pilot billing period (all usage lines). If you prefer it to apply only to incremental delta (High‑Throughput over Compact costs) we can model that; typically customers like a full invoice credit for simplicity.

3) Retention: 90‑day is default and included. Moving to 1 year requires a storage add‑on; that is an opt‑in line item and doesn't require a legal amendment for the pilot period, but procurement should expect a subscription addendum for multi‑year retention.

Worked example (monthly snapshot):
- Compact baseline: 10M tokens = $1,200
- High‑Throughput during spike (estimated 20% total time): incremental cost = $1,800
- Gross invoice = $3,000
- Pilot credit (15%) = -$450
- Net = $2,550

If you want the credit applied only to incremental cost the net would be $3,000 - ($1,800 * 0.15) = $2,730. Spreadsheet attached: redwood_feature_matrix.xlsx includes the per‑route breakouts and the downgrade credit schedule.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_feature_matrix.xlsx (pricing examples, downgrade schedule)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot

Team —

Two legal/procurement points for the playbook: 
- Emergency rollback amendment: we will include a short amendment template that grants the 10‑minute protected route rollback and documents the operational fee for out‑of‑band manual rollbacks. This can be an addendum to the SOW (no full contract re‑negotiation).
- Pilot credit: include a clause that the 15% pilot credit is applied as a one‑time invoice credit within the pilot billing period and does not carry forward after pilot expiration unless otherwise agreed.

Priya — can you prepare a one‑page amendment and an example invoice line for procurement? I suggest also including a PO acceptance clause (Net 30 standard) and a contact for urgent operations (ops@redwood.com).

Lauren Bishop
Director, Contracts & Commercials
lauren@redwood.com
From: Amira Patel <amira@zenithhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Cross-tier swap checklist and fallbacks for Zenith Health pilot

Vivek/Ben/Lauren —

This is great — thank you. Procurement reviewed Ben's worked example and prefers the pilot credit applied to the full invoice (simpler for PO reconciliation). Procurement will issue a PO for the pilot coverage (3 weeks active, 3 weeks evaluation) once we get the one‑page amendment and sample invoice. Expect a PO by Friday.

A couple of final asks before PO: 
- Please include the protected endpoints list and confirm the 10‑minute automated rollback will be enforced for those routes.
- Can you add a line on expected SLA behavior during a tier swap (e.g., expected 95th percentile latency change)? We need that for our risk register.

I'll attach a PO intent email from procurement if helpful.

Best,
Amira Patel
Director of Product, Zenith Health
amira@zenithhealth.com
